Oracle Fusion Cloud 26C: what changed

148 changes we track: the most relevant ones, up to 25 per module family (out of 786 features, by our count, in the 26C What's New documents for Financials, Procurement, SCM, Logistics, Projects and HCM). See the 26C what-to-test checklist →

Impact on upgrade is our editorial rating of how much a change affects existing users and testing; Oracle scale is Oracle's own rating. Always confirm details on the linked Oracle page.

By module family: Financials (25) · HCM (25) · Logistics (OTM, GTM, WMS) (25) · Procurement (25) · Project Management (23) · Supply Chain & Manufacturing (25) · Former opt-ins now standard in 26C (36)

Get the 26D checklist now: what switches on by itself, which former opt-ins are now standard, what to test

Inside the free 26D checklist (PDF):

  • The 23 opt-ins Oracle lists as ending with 26D: 9 switch on for everyone, 14 need setup
  • 9 HCM Redwood default switches and other HCM notices for 26D
  • 9 baseline regression checks, plus typical 26D test and production dates by cohort

Then one plain-English email per Oracle quarterly update, linked to Oracle's docs. Free. 4 emails a year plus short opt-in alerts. Unsubscribe anytime. Read issue #1 (26C) → · Privacy

In short: 26C is the current Oracle Fusion Cloud quarterly update. We track 148 of its changes in plain English, out of 786 features (our count) in Oracle's 26C What's New documents for the modules we cover. 120 of the 148 are delivered switched on and 16 are rated high impact on upgrade. Oracle's opt-in expiration list names 36 former opt-ins now standard in 26C: 14 switched on for everyone, 22 need setup.

Invoice Import with Supplier Bank Account Details Using Collaboration Messaging Framework

Impact on upgrade: highOracle scale: Larger scaleAutomatically onFinancialsFinancials · Payables Invoice ProcessingIdea Lab
B2B XML invoices imported into Payables through Collaboration Messaging can now carry the supplier's remit-to bank account number and IBAN, and the invoice installment is paid to that account. If the bank details are left out, Payables falls back to the supplier's primary bank account.
Oracle's "Impact to Existing Processes": Larger scale · Action to enable: None · Oracle source

Impact on upgrade: lowOracle scale: Small scaleAutomatically onFinancialsFinancials · Asset Acquisition, Maintenance, and LeaseIdea Lab

Oracle's "Impact to Existing Processes": Small scale · Action to enable: None · Oracle source

Frequently asked questions

How many features are in Oracle's 26C What's New?

786 features by our count, in the 26C What's New documents for Financials, Procurement, Supply Chain, Logistics, Project Management and HCM. We summarise 148 of them in plain English: the most relevant ones, up to 25 per module family.

Which 26C changes switch on automatically?

120 of the 148 26C changes we track are delivered switched on. 62 of those are rated medium or high impact on upgrade and are listed in section 2 of the 26C what-to-test checklist. Use the enablement filter above to see them all.

Which former opt-ins are now standard in 26C?

Oracle's Current Opt-In Expirations list names 36 features whose opt-in period ended with 26C: 14 are switched on for everyone and 22 need setup if you want to use them. See the list.

How many 26C changes are rated high impact?

16 of the 148 changes we track. Impact on upgrade is our editorial rating of how much a change affects existing users and testing; Oracle's own scale rating is shown separately on each change.

What should I test for 26C?

Start with the 26C what-to-test checklist: baseline regression checks based on Oracle's guidance, the changes delivered switched on, the former opt-ins now standard, and Oracle's IMPORTANT Actions and Considerations for each product.
